questions.stem: The Tabla is classified under which category of Indian musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Indian instruments are classified into 4 categories (Natya Shastra by Bharat Muni): (1) TATA VADYA = string (Sitar, Sarod, Veena, Sarangi, Santoor); (2) SUSHIR VADYA = wind (Bansuri, Shehnai, Nadaswaram, Shankh); (3) AVANADDHA VADYA = percussion with stretched membrane (Tabla, Mridangam, Dholak, Pakhawaj); (4) GHANA VADYA = solid/self-sounding, no strings or membrane (Manjira, Ghatam, Kartal, Jaltarang). Tabla was developed in the 18th c., reportedly by Amir Khusrau's disciple — hence it's relatively recent compared to Pakhawaj.

questions.stem: The Shehnai, associated with Ustad Bismillah Khan, is what type of instrument?
questions.explanation: The Shehnai is a SUSHIR (wind/reed) instrument — a double-reed oboe-family instrument made of wood with a metal flared bell. Traditionally played at weddings, temples, and on auspicious occasions in North India; considered a symbol of auspiciousness ('mangal vadya'). The legendary Ustad BISMILLAH KHAN (1916-2006) — Bharat Ratna 2001 — was the Shehnai's greatest modern exponent; he played at Red Fort on 15 August 1947. South Indian counterpart: NADASWARAM (longer, louder, always played outdoors).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who among the following was the world-famous SANTOOR exponent from Jammu & Kashmir, awarded the Padma Vibhushan?
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma (1938-2022) single-handedly elevated the Santoor — a Kashmiri folk trapezoidal string instrument played with mallets, with 100 strings — to the status of an Indian classical concert instrument. Padma Shri 1991, Padma Vibhushan 2001. Known for the 'Shiv-Hari' duo with Hariprasad Chaurasia (composed music for Silsila, Chandni, Lamhe). Ravi Shankar = Sitar, Zakir Hussain = Tabla, Hariprasad Chaurasia = Bansuri (bamboo flute).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Mridangam is the principal percussion instrument of which classical music tradition?
questions.explanation: The Mridangam is the primary percussion instrument of Carnatic classical music (South India) — a barrel-shaped two-headed drum played horizontally, with the right head higher pitched (valanthalai) and left lower (thoppi). Its counterpart in Hindustani (North India) classical music is the PAKHAWAJ (from which the Mridangam evolved). The Mridangam's Carnatic equivalents: Ghatam (clay pot), Kanjira (tambourine), Morsing (jaw harp). Palghat Mani Iyer, TK Murthy, Umayalpuram Sivaraman are legendary exponents.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Trinity of Carnatic Music refers to which three 18th-century composers?

options.option_text: Mysore Vasudevacharya, GN Balasubramaniam, MS Subbulakshmi

questions.explanation: The Carnatic Trinity are three composer-saints — all contemporaries born in Tiruvarur (Tamil Nadu) in the 18th c.: (1) TYAGARAJA (1767-1847) — composed 700+ kritis in Telugu; Aradhana celebrated at Thiruvaiyaru; (2) MUTHUSWAMI DIKSHITAR (1775-1835) — Sanskrit kritis, Navagraha kritis on planets; (3) SHYAMA SHASTRI (1762-1827) — Telugu/Sanskrit works, specialist of the Swarajathi form. Purandara Dasa (~1484-1564) is called the 'Sangeet Pitamaha' (father of Carnatic) — separate, earlier figure.

questions.stem: The Pena (a bowed, single-stringed folk instrument with a coconut shell resonator) is a cultural symbol of which state?
questions.explanation: The PENA (also called Bana or Tingtelia) is a traditional single-stringed bowed chordophone of Manipur, made of a coconut-shell resonator covered with dry leather and a bamboo neck. Central to the Meitei people's cultural repertoire — especially accompanying the narration of the Khamba-Thoibi legend. Pena artists are called 'Pena Asheiba'. Other state-specific folk instruments worth knowing: PEPA (buffalo-horn flute — Assam's Bihu), GOGONA (reed-jaw harp — Assam), DHOL (Assam, Punjab etc.), BIHU DHOL, SUMUI (Manipur flute), DIMSA & RABAB (tribal).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Amir Khusrau is credited with inventing which two Indian musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Amir Khusrau (1253-1325), the court poet-musician of the Delhi Sultanate, is traditionally credited with having developed or popularised the SITAR (from the Persian 'seh-tar' = three-stringed — evolved from Veena + Persian tanbur) and — per one tradition — the TABLA (though codification of modern tabla is by Siddhar Khan, 18th c., disciple of Khusrau's lineage). Khusrau also developed the Qawwali and Khayal genres, ragas like Yaman, Aiman, Bahar, Sanam. He is called 'Tuti-e-Hind' (Parrot of India).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which Hindustani gharana is the OLDEST traditional gharana of classical vocal music?
questions.explanation: The GWALIOR gharana is the oldest school of Hindustani khayal singing, traced to Natthan Pir Baksh (late 18th c.) and the Haddu-Hassu brothers. Known for pure raga-based khayal, clear enunciation. Other major gharanas: AGRA (Ustad Faiyaz Khan — blend of khayal with dhrupad), JAIPUR-ATRAULI (Alladiya Khan — rare ragas, complex tans), KIRANA (Abdul Karim Khan, Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal — emphasis on swara and mood), PATIALA (Bade Ghulam Ali Khan — thumri + khayal), RAMPUR-SAHASWAN (Mushtaq Husain Khan), BHENDIBAZAAR (Mumbai — influenced by Agra). Tabla has its own gharanas: Delhi, Lucknow, Ajrada, Farrukhabad, Benaras, Punjab.

questions.stem: Sarod is an adaptation of which Central Asian instrument, brought to India and evolved?
questions.explanation: The Sarod is a modified descendant of the Afghan RABAB, brought by Afghan warriors and refined in Gwalior during the 19th c. Unlike the wooden-fretted sitar, the Sarod has a fretless fingerboard covered with a steel plate and uses a coconut-shell resonator — giving it a deep, meditative tone. The GHULAM ALI KHAN / ALI AKBAR KHAN / AMJAD ALI KHAN lineage and the MAIHAR gharana (Ustad Allauddin Khan) are principal exponents. The original Afghan Rabab is also played in Kashmiri music; Sitar evolved from Persian Tanbur/Setar.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Ghana Vadya (self-sounding) instrument?
questions.explanation: GHANA VADYA = self-sounding (idiophones): MANJIRA (small cymbals), GHATAM (clay pot, Carnatic), GHUNGROO (ankle bells), KHARTAL (wooden clappers), CHIMTA (metal tongs), JALTARANG (tuned bowls of water). SARANGI is a TATA VADYA (bowed string) — played with a bow; main accompaniment for Hindustani vocal music and Kathak. Its smaller bamboo cousin, the DILRUBA & ESRAJ, are also strings. Students often confuse Sarangi with Sarod (plucked) and the wind instruments — these are distinct classifications.
